본문: I've been trying to get better about regularly going to a salon for a hair cut. For years I just went to Great Clips once a year. Basically, I'd go whenever I hated my hair so I'd have to chop inches off of split ends. But now I have a salon and a hair stylist I love so I'm trying to go every 3 or so months. My stylist recommended that I start using a hair diffuser whenever I dry my hair because I have naturally curly hair. I don't use heat on my hair often but when I do, I've been attaching this to my hair dryer. I have the Infiniti Pro by Conair 1875 Watt Full Size Salon Performance AC Motor Styler/Hair Dryer (that I also bought from Amazon) and this fits on it perfectly. I read reviews that sometimes this hair diffuser doesn't work on all hair dryers because the diameter is smaller or larger than what this is compatible. But I measured the diameter of my hair dryer so I knew it would work. And I love how my hair reacts to being diffused. My curls just look marvelous. I almost wish I had time to blow dry my hair every day - almost. I love how it's collapsible so it doesn't take up too much space under my sink. I definitely recommend this product if you're looking for a diffuser.

It came right on time, with Prime 2-day shipping. But it came in a plastic baggie with the Curly Co logo on it. No product box, no instructions. Granted, I could be the only nerd out there who needs instructions on how to attach and use a diffuser. It was mostly the attaching that I needed help with. It was very difficult to attach to my blowdryer (a travel size Revlon, I think? I'm not sure, I originally bought it for helping my watercolor dry faster), and feels like it might slip off. To attach, I ended up putting the diffuser on the floor, pressing the barrel of my blowdryer into the attachment tube, and sort of peeling the attachment onto the dryer. My fingers got pinched and scraped in the process, and I pretty much had to put my full bodyweight into it. If my partner had been home, I would have asked him to do it since he used to throw people for fun (cheerleader) and would have had the required strength in one arm. Even so, it took me a solid 5 minutes of bodyweight and a few minutes of Googling to figure out if maybe the diffuser just wouldn't work with my dryer, or if I was doing it wrong. I haven't used the diffuser yet. It just got here 10 minutes ago. I'll update when I've used it a few times. **EDIT** I've now used this diffuser twice. It stays on well enough while I'm using it, but as someone else mentioned: collapsible means holding the diffuser the whole time anyway, because it keeps collapsing during use. Also, be prepared to go through the painful process of reattaching it EVERY time you want to use it. When I lay my dryer down when I'm done, at least 1/3 of the edge of the diffuser slips off the barrel every time. And although I no longer need to use my bodyweight and I've tried other ways of attaching the diffuser, the only one that works is getting my fingers in the silicone attachment ring of the diffuser and stretching it over my dryer. Doesn't sound like a big deal, but this material doesn't stretch well-- as a result, my index fingers and thumbs are visibly scraped, and one index nail got smashed between diffuser and dryer hard enough that one side of the nail is detached and bleeding. A+ job making this "universal" diffuser attachable by the women it's meant for, dev team!

It fits my hair dryer perfectly and stores away nicely (it also allows me to give my old, faithful diffuser a break!). The basket portion of the diffuser is generously wide, so styling is easy as it feels like it is cradling my hair. I use low heat, or no heat, and my curls come great with every use. The materials used are light, yet sturdy. Last but not least, the price.. it's a great value for the price. It fits on my Revlon 1875 Infrared, which has a notoriously weirdly-shaped barrel, and actually does a good job diffusing, almost surprisingly so. Obviously you'll have to handle it a bit more gingerly than a normal, non-collapsing diffuser, but for the price - and for not having to take up precious suitcase space - I'll deal. Would I go insane if this was my daily use diffuser? Probably, but for the purpose of using it a few times a year while traveling, it'll do just fine.

I have fine, curly hair, and use a Conair dryer with attached diffuser every day at home. I purchased this collapsible diffuser to use exclusively with my travel blow dryer (https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B00006IV22/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_2?th=1) when traveling, and have used it a few times now. Overall, it works like it's supposed to and takes up a lot less space compared to my every-day diffuser. Some other reviewers commented about the tight fit when putting the diffuser on. I also had a hard time with this, but once it was on there wasn't a problem. Other commenters also mentioned the diffuser collapsing. I didn't have a problem with this, but I tend to hold the diffuser and not the dryer while I'm drying my hair. However, it isn't sturdy enough to lift my hair at the roots like my every-day, non-collapsible diffuser is. Pros: compact design (collapses to about an inch); light; easy to remove from dryer and collapse; diffuses the air like it's supposed to. Cons: a little hard to fit over the dryer nozzle; not as sturdy compared to non-collapsible diffusers; not strong enough to lift the hair at the roots for drying.
